title: Library hours change
text:
CAMPUS LIBRARY: EXAM PERIOD HOURS
From December 4 to December 15, the library will be open 24 hours a day, Monday to Friday. Weekend hours are 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. A valid student ID is required to enter between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. Group study rooms can be booked online for up to three hours at a time.

questions.stem: When must students show an ID to enter the library?
questions.explanation: A valid student ID is required between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.

questions.stem: How long can a group study room be booked at one time?
questions.explanation: Rooms can be booked for up to three hours at a time.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the library outside the exam period?
choices: It is usually not open 24 hours a day
It does not have group study rooms
questions.explanation: Special 24-hour opening for the exam period suggests the usual hours are shorter.

title: Message from a professor
text:
Subject: Change to Thursday's class

Dear students,
I have to attend a meeting on Thursday morning, so our 10 a.m. class will move to 2 p.m. in Room 214 instead of our usual room. The reading for the week has not changed. If you cannot attend at the new time, please email me by Wednesday so I can share my notes with you.
Best wishes,
Professor Okafor

questions.stem: Why did the professor write this email?
choices: To announce a change of time and room
To ask students to attend a meeting
questions.explanation: The class moves to 2 p.m. in Room 214.

questions.stem: What should a student do who cannot come at 2 p.m.?
questions.explanation: Students who cannot attend should email by Wednesday.

questions.stem: What does the professor suggest about the reading?
choices: Students should still do it for Thursday
It will be discussed by email
questions.explanation: "The reading for the week has not changed" implies students should prepare as usual.

title: Dining hall specials
text:

Breakfast (7 to 10 a.m.): pancakes, fruit, eggs any style
Lunch (11:30 a.m. to 2 p.m.): vegetable curry with rice; grilled chicken sandwich; soup of the day: tomato
Dinner (5 to 8 p.m.): pasta bar; salmon with green beans

questions.stem: At what time does lunch end?

title: Bike parking
text:
NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS
Bicycles may no longer be left in building hallways, as they block emergency exits. Please use the new covered racks behind Hall B. Bikes left in hallways after March 1 will be moved to the storage room, and owners must collect them from the front desk with ID.

questions.stem: Why are bicycles no longer allowed in hallways?
questions.explanation: Bikes in hallways block emergency exits.

questions.stem: What will probably happen to a bike left in a hallway on March 5?
choices: It will be moved to the storage room
It will be moved behind Hall B
questions.explanation: Bikes left after March 1 will be moved to the storage room.

title: Tutor wanted
text:
WANTED: Math tutor for a high school student
Two evenings a week, 6 to 7:30 p.m., near Central Park station. Must be confident with algebra and geometry. Previous tutoring experience preferred but not required. $25 per hour. Please send a short message about yourself to the email below.

questions.stem: Which requirement is stated as necessary?
questions.explanation: *Must be confident with algebra and geometry*; experience is only preferred.

questions.stem: How many hours a week is the job?
questions.explanation: Two evenings of an hour and a half each make three hours.

title: Campus shuttle
text:
CAMPUS SHUTTLE: WEEKDAY SERVICE
Main Gate to Science Park: every 15 minutes, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Science Park to Main Gate: every 15 minutes, 7:10 a.m. to 7:10 p.m.
Evening service (7 p.m. to midnight): every 30 minutes, both directions.
No weekend service during the summer term.

questions.stem: How often does the shuttle run at 9 p.m. on a weekday?
questions.explanation: Evening service from 7 p.m. to midnight runs every 30 minutes.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the summer term?
choices: Students cannot take the shuttle on weekends
questions.explanation: There is no weekend service during the summer term.

title: Club meeting
text:
Subject: Photography club this Friday

Hi everyone,
This Friday we'll meet at the main entrance at 4 p.m. for a photo walk around the old town. Bring your camera or phone, and wear comfortable shoes. If it rains, we'll meet in Room 3C instead and look at last month's photos. Snacks will be provided!
See you there,
Lena

questions.stem: What will happen if it rains?
choices: The club will meet in Room 3C
questions.explanation: If it rains, they will meet in Room 3C and look at photos.

questions.stem: What are members asked to bring?
choices: A map of the old town
questions.explanation: Bring your camera or phone; snacks are provided.

title: Water shut-off
text:
MAINTENANCE NOTICE
Water to Buildings 4 and 5 will be turned off on Tuesday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. while pipes are repaired. Please store some water for drinking beforehand. Showers in the sports center will remain open. We apologize for the inconvenience.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To warn residents of a temporary water shut-off
To ask residents to repair pipes
questions.explanation: It announces that water will be off on Tuesday morning.

questions.stem: Where can residents shower during the repairs?
questions.explanation: Showers in the sports center will remain open.

title: Group project
text:
Sam: Hey, are we still meeting at 3 to finish the slides?
Priya: Yes, but can we do the library instead of the café? Too noisy there.
Sam: Sure. I'll book a room. Can you bring the charts?
Priya: Already done. I'll send them now so you can check them first.

questions.stem: Why does Priya want to change the meeting place?

questions.stem: What will Priya probably do next?
questions.explanation: *I'll send them now.*

title: Phone repair shop
text: Fast and friendly service. My screen was cracked and they replaced it in under an hour. The price was a little higher than I expected, but they explained why and gave me a three-month guarantee. I would go back. Four stars.

questions.stem: How does the writer feel about the shop overall?
questions.explanation: Fast, friendly, would go back, four stars: mostly positive, with one small complaint.

questions.stem: What did the shop give the writer?
questions.explanation: *Gave me a three-month guarantee.*

title: Lost and found
text: FOUND in Lecture Hall 2 on Monday: one black umbrella, a blue water bottle and a silver laptop charger. Items can be collected from the Student Services desk on weekdays from 9 to 5. Unclaimed items will be donated to charity after 30 days.

questions.stem: What happens to items that are not collected?
choices: They are thrown away after a week
questions.explanation: Unclaimed items will be donated to charity after 30 days.

title: Apartment viewing
text:
Subject: Viewing the apartment on Elm Street

Hello,
Thank you for your interest in the apartment. You are welcome to view it on Saturday at 11 a.m. The rent is $900 a month, including water but not electricity. A deposit of one month's rent is due when you sign the lease. Please reply to confirm the time.
Regards,
M. Torres

questions.stem: Which cost is NOT included in the rent?
questions.explanation: Rent includes water but not electricity.

questions.stem: How much is the deposit?
questions.explanation: A deposit of one month's rent, $900.

questions.stem: What will a new tenant probably have to pay when signing the lease?
choices: The deposit, in addition to rent
Nothing until the end of the month
questions.explanation: The deposit of one month's rent is due at signing.
